bull.b: Rapid DTC growth and a record share of sales show that On is strengthening control over customer experience and channel economics. A larger owned-channel base can support brand consistency and mix quality over the next several quarters, while reducing reliance on third-party retail execution.

Gross margin above 65% and EBITDA near 20%, alongside improved TTM net margin, demonstrate that growth is translating into meaningful profitability. Management's reiterated targets provide a near-term framework for sustaining attractive economics as the company expands products, regions, and DTC penetration.

Strong TTM operating and free cash flow, with FCF at roughly 83% of net income, gives On internal funding capacity for stores, innovation, and international expansion. Moderate leverage and strong ROE further support financial flexibility, although cash conversion has varied historically.

bear.b: Wholesale growth is slowing, particularly in the Americas, where promotional conditions and weaker sell-through are affecting everyday running franchises. Even if the channel reset protects full-price positioning, reduced sell-in and retailer volatility can constrain revenue cadence and make near-term growth more dependent on DTC execution.

Inventory rose about 30% while management calibrated wholesale sell-in. Although attributed mainly to volume growth and foreign-exchange effects, elevated stock raises the execution burden: slower sell-through could require more disciplined replenishment or weigh on working-capital efficiency.

Higher U.S. import tariffs are an external pressure on the cost structure, and the timing of expected refunds is uncertain. Because refunds were excluded from Q2 results and full-year margin outlook, near-term cash and margin outcomes may remain less predictable as the policy impact develops.
